Hard to see from the inside.

The way decisions get made, the way people talk to each other (or don't), the way work gets done around here: all of it made perfect sense when you built it. Then the company grew, and the habits that held everything together when you were ten people started getting in the way at forty.

In twenty years, I have never once walked into a company where the problem started with bad intentions. It almost always starts with good ones, and the habits that grew up quietly around them.

Here's what it tends to look like.

  • Bigger customers and new opportunities pulling the company in new directions.
  • Good people promoted into leadership, and you're figuring out how to develop them as you go.
  • Meetings that end with a decision, and then everyone goes back to what they were already doing.
  • Problems between people that keep landing on your desk.
  • Someone who's been loyal to you in a role they can't grow into, and everyone can feel it.
  • Too much of the strategy lives only in your head.

    Bring Dr. J in

The higher you climb, the fewer people tell you the truth.

Your team watches what you react to and brings you what you want to hear, because their jobs depend on you. Your family wants you to be certain. Your customers have become friends, your peers are often your competitors, and everyone knows the image you've got to keep up. Somewhere along the way you ran out of people who will say the hard thing out loud.

That's the role I've played for twenty years with owners and their teams. I listen for what people aren't saying, I understand how a company runs, and I know how to walk people through the hard parts instead of around them.

You don't have to filter with me, and I won't filter with you.
